The poshest dog to arrive at Battersea is Luke the rough collie, and he's not used to slumming it, while exhausted new mum Fifi is old before her time thanks to her many pregnancies, and no-one can believe she's only two years old.

Alex tours northern Sicily, revealing a different side to this ancient island. She visits a palace in Palermo, samples the street food and meets a group of locals determined to change the mafia's influence over island life.

Supply teacher Wilson makes an impression on Janeece, but panic ensues when the pair disappear and the truth about Wilson is revealed. Meanwhile, Eddie confronts Rachel about her past and issues her an ultimatum.

Maggie and Phil can't keep their hands off each other, but James still isn't doing any revision and they have started to worry. Phil thinks Maggie should give up her job to help and she hands in her notice. Then she discovers that Phil and Brian's overtime has centred round a singles bar and a lap-dancing club, and she puts her foot down. Elsewhere, Brenda has a fall.
Julia realises she's in love with Benjamin. Patrick and Della, who are suspicious of Benjamin, follow him and catch him in a compromising situation. Is he really who he seems?
Charming, witty comedy drama, inspired by the best-selling novel by Marian Keyes, of what happens when a tangled web of deceit pitches one woman, two men and a baby into a romantic minefield.

The police are sent to investigate a theft from a fur factory and Greengrass thinks he has found gold with his metal detector.

A farmer is found dead, and for the local police inspector it's clear that the man's son, James McCarthy, should be charged with the murder. Although for Alice Turner, McCarthy's childhood friend, the matter is not a murder but a mystery, and she sends a telegram to Sherlock Holmes. As Holmes takes up the case, Alice becomes a vital source of information.

The four major soaps - 'Coronation Street', 'EastEnders', 'Emmerdale' and 'Hollyoaks' - go head-to-head for the coveted awards.
